name: Table
summary: Use a table to let users compare structured data across rows and columns.
whenToUse: Use when information has consistent row and column relationships that users need to compare.
Use numeric column classes for numbers that benefit from right alignment and tabular figures.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a table for page layout.
Do not use for a simple key-value record; use a Summary list.
Do not put unrelated content into columns only to save vertical space.

anatomy.name: Table and caption
anatomy.description: A govuk-table has a descriptive caption, which may be visually hidden if an equivalent heading is already present.

anatomy.name: Column headings
anatomy.description: A thead uses th scope=col for each column label.

anatomy.name: Body rows
anatomy.description: Rows contain th scope=row where the first cell identifies the row, followed by data cells.

variants.name: Numeric columns
variants.use: Values such as prices, counts and measurements that should align by digit.

behaviour: The table has no GOV.UK JavaScript behaviour.
For narrow screens, simplify columns or provide an intentional responsive treatment without changing relationships.
If sorting is added, use a separately tested accessible pattern; base GOV.UK Table is not sortable.
accessibility: Provide a caption and use scope attributes so headers are associated with their data.
Keep a logical source order and do not rely on colour or position alone for meaning.
Avoid horizontal scrolling for ordinary data; when unavoidable, keep keyboard access and visible context.
content: Use concise column headings with consistent units and formatting.
Align comparable numeric values and include currency or measurement units clearly.
Do not leave ambiguous empty cells; use meaningful text when absence itself matters.
